title: DocumentReleaseMemberManifest
description: The one global member manifest of a DocumentRelease v2 bundle. v2 does not partition the RELEASE; every member is listed here, sorted by objectKey. Tabular members are JSONL and the `text/` and `blobs/` members are partition buckets, so a large mint's manifest is tens of members rather than one per text body. A bucket holding several text bodies is recoverable only through the `text-body-index` member, whose row shape this schema also owns — an index over member bytes is a fact about how members are packed, which is this manifest's business and no row schema's. The member-descriptor protocol is identical to SourceCatalogRelease v1's; only the role and media-type vocabularies differ.

memberDescriptor.description: One immutable file inside the bundle. objectKey is a relative POSIX path; no absolute path, no parent traversal, no symlink.

recordCount.description: Stated per ROLE, not per "has rows": null for a `schema` member, which is one document rather than a stream; the row count for a tabular member and for the `text-body-index`; and the number of text bodies in the bucket for a partitioned `rendition` or `representation` member, which IS a bucket of rows exactly as the catalog's partitions are. The old null-for-rendition rule described an unpartitioned layout that no longer exists.

schemaId.description: The schema governing this member's rows, or the media contract for an opaque member. A `text-body-index` member names THIS schema: its row shape is `$defs/textBodyIndexRow` below.

textBodyIndexRow.description: One text body's byte slice inside one partitioned member. Digest-bucketed `text/` and `blobs/` members hold whatever bodies hash into them, and without this row nothing recovers one body's bytes from a bucket it shares — no other field in this format carries an offset into a member. With it, every body's slice is addressable and digest-verifiable from bundle bytes alone, so the refusal to mint a multi-body bucket lifts wherever the index covers that bucket. A slice whose bytes do not digest to `sha256` is `invalid.member-digest`, exactly as a whole member's would be.

family.description: Which partition family the member belongs to: `text` for a selected representation, `blob` for a captured rendition. One text body has one slice in each family it is present in.

member.description: The declared `objectKey` of the partitioned member this slice lies in. A relative POSIX path, and a member the manifest lists.

startByte.description: Half-open [startByte, startByte + byteLength) over the member's bytes.

sha256.description: Digest of exactly those slice bytes, so a consumer verifies the body it extracted rather than the bucket it came from.
